candidates.title: AdminClient 컨슈머 그룹 관리
candidates.concept_granularity: single family of AdminClient operations that read and modify consumer groups and their committed offsets, motivated by reprocessing after a fault or in disaster recovery

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리

candidates.title: listConsumerGroups()
candidates.concept_granularity: single listing operation whose valid() yields only the groups the cluster returned without error, with errors() and all() offering the two other error dispositions

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 조회

candidates.title: describeConsumerGroups()
candidates.concept_granularity: single detail operation returning a group's members, their identifiers and hosts, their assigned partitions, the assignment algorithm and the coordinator host

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 조회

candidates.title: 컨슈머 랙
candidates.concept_granularity: single measure of how far a consumer group trails the newest message, absent from the group description and obtainable through AdminClient instead of by parsing the internal commit topic

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 조회

candidates.title: listConsumerGroupOffsets()
candidates.concept_granularity: single operation returning one group's topic partitions mapped to their last committed offsets, scoped to a single group unlike describeConsumerGroups

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 조회

candidates.title: listOffsets()
candidates.concept_granularity: single operation resolving a partition offset by specification - earliest, latest or the first record written after a timestamp

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 조회

candidates.title: alterConsumerGroupOffsets()
candidates.concept_granularity: single offset-modification operation, the most used of the group-modifying methods, which Kafka refuses while the group is running

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 수정
## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 수정

candidates.title: 커밋된 오프셋 삭제
candidates.concept_granularity: single reset technique that is unreliable because a consumer finding no committed offset falls back on auto.offset.reset, making an explicit rewind to the earliest offset the deterministic choice

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 수정

candidates.title: 오프셋 토픽 값 전파
candidates.concept_granularity: single propagation rule under which a group reads the offset topic only when a consumer is newly assigned or started, which is why Kafka forbids modifying a running group's offsets

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 수정

candidates.title: 상태를 가진 애플리케이션의 오프셋 리셋
candidates.concept_granularity: single hazard in which rewinding offsets without clearing an application's accumulated state double-counts the reprocessed range

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 수정

candidates.title: UnknownMemberIdException
candidates.concept_granularity: single failure mode raised when a live group's coordinator treats an offset change as a commit from a non-member, with stopping the consumer application the only remedy

locators.heading: ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 > ### 컨슈머 그룹 수정

candidates.title: describeCluster()
candidates.concept_granularity: single metadata read exposing the cluster id, its broker nodes and the controller, information Kafka clients otherwise abstract away

locators.heading: ## 클러스터 메타데이터

candidates.title: 토픽에 파티션 추가
candidates.concept_granularity: single rare and risky operation, since a topic's partition count is normally fixed at creation and widening it breaks the assumption that one key always lands on one partition

locators.heading: ## 고급 어드민 작업 > ### 토픽에 파티션 추가

candidates.title: createPartitions()
aliases: 파티션 추가 후 총 개수 지정
candidates.concept_granularity: single expansion operation taking the partition count the topic should end up with rather than the number to add, so the current count must be read first

locators.heading: ## 고급 어드민 작업 > ### 토픽에 파티션 추가

candidates.title: deleteRecords()
candidates.concept_granularity: single operation marking every record older than a given offset unreadable to consumers, with the physical erase happening asynchronously afterwards

locators.heading: ## 고급 어드민 작업 > ### 토픽에서 레코드 삭제
## 고급 어드민 작업 > ### 토픽에서 레코드 삭제

candidates.title: 선호 리더 선출
candidates.concept_granularity: single election that restores each partition's designated preferred replica as leader, which Kafka checks every five minutes and which electLeaders() can trigger on demand

locators.heading: ## 고급 어드민 작업 > ### 리더 선출

candidates.title: 언클린 리더 선출
candidates.concept_granularity: single election promoting a replica that is not eligible to lead, trading the loss of events never replicated from the old leader for the partition's availability

locators.heading: ## 고급 어드민 작업 > ### 리더 선출

candidates.title: electLeaders()
candidates.concept_granularity: single asynchronous election call whose return precedes cluster-wide awareness, so describeTopics may disagree and a multi-partition request may partly succeed

locators.heading: ## 고급 어드민 작업 > ### 리더 선출

candidates.title: 레플리카 재할당
candidates.concept_granularity: single operation placing each of a partition's replicas on a chosen broker, used to relieve an overloaded broker, add replicas, drain a machine or isolate hot topics

locators.heading: ## 레플리카 재할당

candidates.title: 재할당 스로틀링
candidates.concept_granularity: single mitigation for the bulk copying a reassignment causes, applying a broker quota - itself readable and writable through AdminClient - to cap replication traffic

locators.heading: ## 레플리카 재할당

candidates.title: NewPartitionReassignment
candidates.concept_granularity: single per-partition instruction whose replica list adds, moves or reorders replicas and whose empty value cancels an in-flight reassignment and restores the prior placement

locators.heading: ## 레플리카 재할당

candidates.title: MockAdminClient
candidates.concept_granularity: single test double standing in for a real cluster, outside the public API and therefore changeable, though its mocked method signatures stay compatible

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: The whole 컨슈머 그룹 관리 section operates on groups.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: Batch 07 asserts what AdminClient does to a consumer group, never what a consumer group is.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: Committed offsets, latest offsets and lag run through the section.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: The offset's definition is applied; these candidates assert how AdminClient reads and rewrites offsets.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L713-716 describes the preferred replica and leader balance.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: Preferred and unclean election are operations over leadership, distinct from the applied definition of a partition leader.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L717 names the setting as the reason to call electLeaders() manually.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: The applied switch already carries its own meaning; this batch points at it.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L656-663 concerns changing a topic's partition count.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: The risk of widening a partition count is a new claim, not a restatement of what a partition is.
Cited as the property the operation endangers, not redefined.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L685 cross-references chap02's segment-size discussion for why records outlive retention.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: The applied concept carries the segment rule; delete-records only points at it.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L682 sets up a 30-day retention requirement.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: Retention is applied; the new claim is that deleteRecords exists for what retention does not remove.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L782 warns about available bandwidth during reassignment.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: The bandwidth concept is applied; throttling relates to it.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L628-631 and L643-647 read cluster id, nodes and controller.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: describeCluster is an operation over the cluster, not a definition of it.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L549-553 asks where a consumer starts when it finds no committed offset.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: The consumer appears as the actor in an example; the claim is about offset deletion.

touch_point_dispositions.evidence: L567 uses a stream application as the stateful example.
touch_point_dispositions.decision_rationale: A passing illustration, not a claim about streams.
